newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds rose mildly across the board in very dull trading on Monday as investors continued to focus on a highly active stock market, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.04 pct to 101.05
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 100.67.
Volume was low at 117 million shekels with tunrover in the Makam falling to only 30 million shekels.
"Trading was very quiet today and bond prices closed only slightly higher," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
"The bond market is less interesting now and investors prefer to focus on the stock market," said another trader.
Long CPI-linked bonds rose mildly with yeilds remaining unchanged.

"The rise of the dollar-linked bonds does not reflect the whole decline of the shekel against the dollar today. I believe that these bonds will continue to rise on Tuesday," the First International trader said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
